item.title: Vallejo announces sports hall of fame inductees
item.description: Instead of the traditional March ceremony, the event will be held this year on Sept. 26 at the Dan Foley Cultural Center. Plenty of time for friends of a dozen athletes and one team to buy tickets.

item.title: Bay Area musician Mingo Lewis dies at 72
item.description: Former Vallejo City Councilmember Tom Bartee says Mingo Lewis was a “kind and fascinating” individual.

item.title: Judge: Deal reached to protect identities of Epstein victims in documents release
item.description: Nearly 100 victims were harmed by sloppy redactions to a massive release of Epstein documents.

item.title: Federal immigration officials scout warehouses as they eye more detention space
item.description: Federal immigration officials are beginning to purchase some warehouses for detention and processing facilities.

item.title: A/E Source: ‘Barefoot in the Park’ debuts Valentine’s weekend
item.description: The show debuts on Friday, Feb. 13, at 8 p.m. at the Bay Area Stage Theatre on Broadway on 515 Broadway St. in Vallejo.

item.title: Trump accused of distorting history of Mexican-American War to justify heavy hand in Latin America
item.description: A social media post by the White House commemorated the anniversary of the war.

item.title: A/E Source: Vacaville teen to perform solo with Solano Symphony Orchestra
item.description: The Solano Symphony Orchestra’s “Salute to Youth” concert will be performed on Sunday, March 22, at 3 p.m. at the Vacaville Performing Arts Theatre.

item.title: Solano Supervisors tackle Black History, zoning, labor issues
item.description: The Solano County Board of Supervisors recognized Black History Month, approved a variety of Zone Text Ammendments and heard from frustrated county employees seeking a new contract. Supervisors Cassandra James and Wanda Williams presented the proclamation naming February as Black History Month in Solano County. item.title: Solano Supervisors hear job losses update
item.description: As layoffs in Solano County climb past 600, county supervisors were briefed Tuesday on the scope of the job losses, the limits of the local job market, and the resources available to workers displaced by recent closures. item.title: Joanna’s voice focus of Vacaville luncheon
item.description: “Our world is so fractured, and any light we can get and shine into darkness is super important,” said club co-president Debi Schrader. “This is a great opportunity to get the message out to people.”
